llm.summary: The skill mostly matches a study-push use case (read local chapter files and schedule daily pushes via a QQ bot), but there are inconsistencies and a few design choices that warrant review before installing (notably a bundled script whose runtime behavior wasn't shown and the skill's ability to use a channels.qqbot config).

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim: deliver daily exam-study items and support chapter/word queries. Declared runtime pieces (references/ files, scripts/daily_push.py, and channels.qqbot config) are consistent with that goal. Minor inconsistencies in SKILL.md's chapter filename mappings vs actual manifest filenames (see examples below) suggest sloppy packaging but do not by themselves indicate malice.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md requires calling the cron tool for any user mention of related phrases and instructs the agent to call scripts/daily_push.py and deliver messages through the 'qqbot' channel to a user's openid. That behavior is coherent for scheduled push messages, but the policy is forceful ("must call cron") and the cron payload references delivering to '{用户的openid}' and a channel config. Review is needed to ensure the script and agent-side cron invocation do not read or leak unrelated data or arbitrary config. Also several filename references in the SKILL.md (chapter mapping) do not match the manifest filenames, which could cause runtime errors.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only) — low installation risk. However a packaged script (scripts/daily_push.py) is included in the bundle; although no install step is required, the agent will execute that script per SKILL.md. The script contents were not shown in the provided excerpt (files truncated), so its network or file-access behavior must be inspected before trusting it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares a required config path channels.qqbot (used to send messages via a QQ bot). That is proportionate for push-delivery features, but channel configs often contain credentials/tokens — granting the skill access to channels.qqbot should be done only if you trust the skill and have inspected scripts/daily_push.py to confirm it only uses the token to send the intended messages and does not exfiltrate other data. No other env vars or unrelated credentials are requested, which is appropriate.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable; the scheduling behavior uses the platform's cron tool as described. This level of persistence and capability (scheduling + sending on a configured channel) is reasonable for a push-notification skill, but combined with the points above it requires code review of the bundled script before enabling scheduled runs.

llm.guidance: Before installing or enabling scheduled runs: (1) Review the bundled script scripts/daily_push.py (it was not included in the truncated files) to confirm it only reads the provided reference markdown files and sends messages via the configured qqbot channel, and that it makes no unexpected network calls or file reads. (2) Inspect your channels.qqbot configuration (it likely contains the bot token) and limit permissions if possible; only grant the minimal channel config needed to send messages. (3) Note the SKILL.md's mandatory rule to always call cron for related user mentions — decide whether you want that enforced behavior, and whether scheduled jobs should run in an isolated session (SKILL.md requests 'sessionTarget': 'isolated', which is good). (4) Fix or ask the author to fix filename mismatches in SKILL.md (several chapter filenames referenced do not match the manifest), otherwise runtime errors may occur. (5) If you are not able to review the script, consider running the skill in a sandboxed agent environment first or decline installation. If you want, provide the full contents of scripts/daily_push.py and I will review it for network/file/exfiltration behavior and other red flags.
